doc: Preregistration for M4 iterations (docs/BUILD_PLAN.md §0.1). One key per iteration under iterations. A key is written once, in its prereg commit, before any of its outcome_paths change; holon audit prereg checks the order and that the key is never edited afterwards. predictions count toward prediction accuracy; regressions are outcomes already recorded in the repo that must not change.

I48.title: Evaluation corpus and unsolved controls: 20 public defects across six fixed systems (two rollups, four beyond), collected by fresh agents from fixed indexes read at snapshots pinned at the prereg (the mechanical ones recomputed by the instrument) and selected mechanically (round robin) from every recorded candidate, doubly labelled with the minimal rule by two different models of one family in fresh tool-less processes from frozen prompts and adjudicated, an isomorphic renaming tool checked by round trip and by independent parsers, and 14 controls with independently computed ground truth sized against pinned budgets

predictions.claim: System spread: under the frozen protocol (fixed indexes, newest first, round-robin selection), at least 4 of the 6 systems contribute at least 3 entries each to the 20, at least 2 of these not rollups (Q20 and the exit ask 3 systems; round robin alone makes one entry from each system with a candidate near certain, so the prediction counts systems with 3 entries).

Inter-rater agreement between two different models of the same family, each prompt read by a fresh tool-less process (labeller a: model A, the family's most capable model available to the build; labeller b: model B, a smaller model of the same family): Cohen's kappa of their primary labels over the nine categories is at least 0.40 (reported, never an exit condition; an undefined kappa is a miss).
The corpus spans the rules: the final labels use at least 5 of the 9 categories, and at most 5 of the 20 entries are labelled none.

Renaming strength: in at least 6 of the 20 entries, at least one identifier the renaming renames (rule N1 fixes exactly which) occurs on a pre-fix line that the fix deletes or changes, so the contamination mitigation reaches the defect's own lines in at least 30% of the corpus.

thresholds.selection: round robin over the systems in the protocol's order, newest fix first within a system (rule C4)
thresholds.agreement: Cohen's kappa over the nine categories with Cohen's standard error and 95% interval, reported (not an exit condition); prediction I48-P2 names a level
thresholds.labellers: labeller a and the adjudicator: model A (the family's most capable model available to the build); labeller b: model B (a smaller, different model of the same family); each prompt read by a fresh tool-less process (corpus_protocol.json labelling_invocation), models recorded only as the tags A and B with the tool's run-time checks; retry rule: cli_error attempts not counted (at most 5, 60 s apart), one more counted attempt after a failed one, no third (Q9: labelled same)
thresholds.renaming: rule N1 (declared in the set; not reserved, with the package-clause names and, in Go files importing "C", every C.X selector name; not exported (a Unicode upper-case initial) or ABI-visible or override; used nowhere outside the set that the checkout shows; in no string or kept comment; in no .sol file of the set solc cannot parse; words Unicode-aware), directives and @solidity/@custom: comments kept, other comments removed and restored; round trip byte for byte; isomorphism by the goast printer, an independent Solidity lexer and the pinned solc 0.8.24
thresholds.indexes: every git index read at a snapshot pinned at the prereg (corpus_protocol.json snapshots: the newest first-parent commit of the branch whose committer date is before the cutoff, for the advisory database, the geth list on branch website of ethereum/go-ethereum, and the four in-repo audit folders), every page at a recorded fetch (final URL and sha256); the mechanical indexes (ghsa, geth) are enumerated and pre-filtered by the instrument's rule, their collectors work from holon eval index's item list, and their fix commits (when the item names a reachable one) and descriptions are checked against the items

I52.title: Baselines on Morph and the corpus pre-fix commits: slither, echidna, medusa, hevm and halmos (pinned under ~/.holon/tools), Go native fuzzing, 2-cycle round-trip testing, frequency-based spec mining and an agent-only review, each at the same budget per target, reported in one findings schema and matched to the labels by location and a blinded match adjudicator; the held-out run is one command, pending I49/I50

predictions.claim: Single-component analyzers find no relational obstruction: none of slither, echidna, medusa, hevm, halmos, go_fuzz and spec_mining detects (located and confirmed) a Morph obstruction of I52_baselines.json relational.ids. Non-vacuity (I52_baselines.json non_vacuity): each baseline named must have status run on at least half of the targets where it applies, else this is a miss.

2-cycle round-trip testing finds the O2 class on Morph and not O1: its bytes cycle on (BatchHeaderV1, BatchHeaderBytes' getters) fails on a version-2 header (byte 0 re-encoded as 1), so two_cycle detects O2; O1 is a Solidity-versus-Go domain difference, a cross-language 2-cycle the baseline has no binding for, so it does not detect O1.

The Solidity analyzers, fuzzers and symbolic executors (slither, echidna, medusa, hevm, halmos) detect no corpus entry. Non-vacuity (I52_baselines.json non_vacuity): each baseline named must have status run on at least half of the targets where it applies, else this is a miss.

Go stock fuzzing and 2-cycle testing (go_fuzz, two_cycle) detect no corpus entry. Non-vacuity (I52_baselines.json non_vacuity): each baseline named must have status run on at least half of the targets where it applies, else this is a miss.

Frequency-based spec mining detects c06 (an unchecked type assertion, a deviation from the package's comma-ok belief) and at most 2 corpus entries in all, and no Morph obstruction. Non-vacuity (I52_baselines.json non_vacuity): each baseline named must have status run on at least half of the targets where it applies, else this is a miss.

The agent-only review at equal budget (one fresh reviewer per system: Morph's scope; the corpus's 20 renamed labelled-file sets together) detects at least 5 of the 20 corpus entries and at least 2 Morph obstructions.
The agent-only review detects more corpus entries than all the other eight baselines together (the size of its detected set exceeds the size of the union of theirs).

The preregistered expected-detection table (thresholds.expected_detections) is right in at least 85% of its cells: one cell per (baseline, corpus entry) where the baseline applies (detected iff listed), and one cell per baseline on Morph (its detected set equals the listed set).

regressions.claim: Construction (the exit): results/eval/morph/<baseline>.json and results/eval/corpus/<baseline>.json exist for all nine baselines, validate against spec/M4/lib/I52_findings.schema.json, name the protocol's sha256, the protocol's budget for the system and the baseline's tool; every target of the system is present, with status not_applicable exactly where the baseline's language is absent from the target, missing only with a missing tool and a reason, error only with a reason, findings sorted with ids f0001.. in order, and a timing file beside each.

Construction (matching): every recorded match is a located pair recomputed by the instrument and every located pair is recorded; exactly the labels with a located finding are adjudicated, each adjudication's confirmed ids a subset of its located ids; located and detected are what the matches and adjudications give.

Equal budget: for every baseline but agent_review, on every target it ran, the units' summed wall clock is at most the system's wall_s plus 60 s, with cpus 1; agent_review: one reviewer per system, its wall clock at most the Morph wall_s (+60) on Morph and 20 x the corpus wall_s (+60) on the corpus, cpu null with its reason. HOLON's own budget is measured by I52_baselines.json holon_budget and compared in the report. The Morph wall_s is the rule's value from results/eval/holon_budget.json (H = M0..M2's recorded from_scratch_gate_s at the base plus M3's measured), and that file's m0..m2 equal the base's records.

Pins: config/holon.json gains a baselines section naming every baseline tool's version and sha256 (missing tools named with a reason), and every one of the 13 existing pins (the bend, lean, replay and hevm entries verify_toolchain.py checks) is byte-identical to the base 4fd64a52; CI's toolchain job does not require the baseline pins.
No M0-M3 outcome changes: no file under results/M0..M3, gen/M0..M3, laws/, replay/, spec/M0..M3 (except none) or audit/ differs from the base 4fd64a52.

Agent blindness: the Morph packet lists only Morph scope files; the corpus packet lists only <entry>/<labelled file> paths of renamed files; each prompt is the frozen template filled in, and no prompt or packet path names holon, the corpus manifest, a label or the fix commit.

morph.wall_s_rule: equal to HOLON's measured Morph budget: wall_s = 60 * ceil(H / 60), H = holon_budget.morph's sum in seconds, written to results/eval/holon_budget.json before any baseline runs

thresholds.heldout: pending I49/I50: python -m holon eval baselines run --system heldout --all
thresholds.non_vacuity: at least half of the applicable targets run
